newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses boosted by Wall St record run.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses boosted by Wall St record run.

text.p: European bourses climbed on Tuesday drawing strength from Wall Street's fourth consecutive record close, which was fuelled by hopes interest rates would not be raised.
On currency markets, the dollar recovered from two-month lows against the mark as Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said he believed a stronger dollar might be more appropriate.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, made the strongest showing registering a 0.3 percent gain by midday. Investors clearly were encouraged by Wall Street but fears over rising British interest rates persisted.
"We are dominated by the U.S. and we have had a predictable mark-up on the back of Wall Street," said a trader. "The gap between us and the Dow is historially very high."

The Dow Jones industrial average finished at 6,255.60 on Monday, eclipsing Friday's record close of 6,219.82. The drive into record territory came as investors bet that interest rates will fall, making stocks even more attractive.
The Dow's latest bull run is the biggest boom since a seven-session record streak in February. Last week's 198-point post-election rally was the second-biggest weekly point gain ever.

The gains have been fuelled by the prospect that the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank will hold monetary policy steady at this Wednesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, good news for business.
Worries of rising British interest rates could continue to hold the market in check, some traders said. Others judged such fears to be unwarranted and were optimistic over prospects for the market.

"The panic over interest rates was overdone," said one trader. "I don't think they are going to push rates up again and if they do it will only be so they can bring them down again ahead of the election," which must be held by next May.
In Frankfurt, floor trading recovered early losses and was showing 0.22 percent gain at midday with investors encouraged by Wall Street. Computerised transactions were also registering gains.
French stocks recovered their composure after slipping in early trade to show marginal gains. Traders said the underlying trend was positive, buoyed by Wall Street's strength.
The dollar recovered from two-month lows against the mark as Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said he believed a stronger dollar might be more appropriate.
The dollar had fallen to fresh two-month lows overnight and weakened against the yen in recent days on the belief U.S. rates are on hold and the economy is slowing.
"The dollar has come up a little...But it has been quite volatile," said a trader at a German bank.
In spite of its recovery, the U.S. currency was at 1.4952 against the mark, slightly down on the levels in late European trading on Monday. It was barely changed against the yen.

Underlying mark strength has also been attributed by some to jitters over the single currency stability pact after Juergen Stark, German state secretary for the finance ministry, said there was no consensus about it.
CURRENCIES AT 1220 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4952 marks and 111.16 yen, compared with 1.4983 marks and 111.20 yen in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1220 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 12.5 points higher at 3,926.9.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 4.47 points at 2,732.79.
PARIS - The CAC 40 index was up 0.31 points at 2205.51
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1220 GMT
Gold was fixed at $381.05 an ounce, compared with $380.75 at the close on Monday. Silver was higher at $4.89, up two cents.
